clue.text: Put an end to spirit

definitions.meaning: to ... a rumour or plan is to stamp it out
whisky distilled in Scotland is a spirit

explanation.surface: Someone stops drinking, or kills off a ghost.
explanation.definitionFit: To scotch means to stop or crush something, and Scotch whisky is a distilled drink.

clue.text: Encourages good health at university

parts.note: cheers is a toast, wishing good health
up means in residence at university, as in 'up at Oxford'

explanation.surface: Someone wishes good health to friends at college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'UP' meaning at university is a British usage: one goes up to Oxford or Cambridge.
explanation.definitionFit: To cheer someone up is to raise their spirits, which encourages them.

clue.text: Patterns varied in one part of church

indicators.note: varied means changed about, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Different designs appear in one part of a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'varied' rearranges the letters of PATTERNS.
explanation.definitionFit: A transept is either arm crossing the nave in a cross-shaped church.

clue.text: A can of worms might well be 12

definitions.meaning: a can of worms is an awkward, troublesome issue
12 across is mashed, and a freshly cooked spud might well be mashed

explanation.surface: A tricky problem may well turn out mashed.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference points to 12 across, MASHED: a cooked spud might well be served mashed.
explanation.definitionFit: A hot potato is a controversial issue nobody wants to handle, like a can of worms.

clue.text: Staff officer finds child when Mum comes in

indicators.note: the words when and Mum come into the middle of the word for child

parts.note: a brat is an unruly child
as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
mum as in 'keep mum' means silence, written SH

explanation.surface: An army staff officer discovers a child on the arrival of its mother.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mum' looks like a mother but means 'be quiet'. Brass hat is old British slang for a senior officer, from the gold braid on the cap.
explanation.definitionFit: A brass hat is slang for a senior officer on the staff, named for the gilt on the cap.

clue.text: Like people who cook fish for tea with bread

indicators.note: to cook figures is to falsify them, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: People who make fish with bread for their tea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cook' rearranges FISH FOR TEA and BREAD; 'with' only joins them. The definition is 'Like people', people who are alike.
explanation.definitionFit: Birds of a feather are similar people, from the proverb that such birds flock together.

clue.text: Contemptuous words 21's associate includes them in vulgar speech

indicators.note: vulgar speech drops the h of has and them, so the phrase is said as a cockney might

parts.note: 21 across is a Channel Island; its neighbour Sark, with includes as has and them as 'em, gives Sark 'as 'em

explanation.surface: Scornful remarks in which an island's partner uses coarse language.
explanation.walkthrough: Sark is another Channel Island, the associate of 21 across. Said with dropped aitches, 'Sark has them' becomes 'Sark 'as 'em'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sarcasm is cutting, mocking language meant to show scorn.

clue.text: American writer, it's said, may …

indicators.note: it's said means the writer's name is spoken, giving a word that sounds like it

parts.note: Nathaniel Hawthorne wrote The Scarlet Letter

explanation.surface: An American author may decline to turn the volume down, read with the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may' looks like a verb but is the definition: may is another name for the hawthorn tree and its blossom.
explanation.definitionFit: May is the common name for hawthorn blossom, and for the shrub itself.

clue.text: refuse to reduce volume

definitions.meaning: to lower the sound by turning a knob

explanation.surface: Completing the previous clue, the author refuses to quieten down.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn down an offer is to reject it; to turn down a radio is to make it quieter.

clue.text: Put off outside the Jug and Bottle

indicators.note: the word for put off sits outside, wrapping the word for the jug

parts.note: to deter is to put off or discourage
the jug and the can are both slang for prison

explanation.surface: A drinker is turned away from the Jug and Bottle, an old name for an off-licence counter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jug and Bottle' reads as a pub's off-sales bar, but 'Jug' is slang for prison and 'Bottle' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A decanter is a glass vessel, a kind of stoppered bottle for serving wine or spirits.

clue.text: Artist giving prize back

indicators.note: back says the word for prize is read from end to start

parts.note: a reward is a prize

explanation.surface: A painter hands a prize back.
explanation.definitionFit: A drawer is one who draws, so a sketching artist.

clue.text: Pictures on walls of recess got damaged

indicators.note: something damaged is knocked out of shape, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Wall paintings in a recess have been damaged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'got damaged' rearranges the letters of OF RECESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Frescoes are paintings done on wet plaster, so they decorate walls.

clue.text: Flirted with mother approaching Slough

indicators.note: the word for mother comes up to and just before the word for slough

parts.note: ma is a familiar name for mother
to slough a skin is to shed it

explanation.surface: Someone flirted with their mother on the way into Slough, the English town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slough' looks like the town west of London but is the verb meaning cast off. To mash is old slang for flirting.
explanation.definitionFit: Mash is dated slang for making amorous advances, so mashed is past-tense flirting.

clue.text: Policy and money buried by Irishman with crimina! record

indicators.note: the word for money is buried inside the name for an Irishman

parts.note: Pat, short for Patrick, is a stock Irishman's name
L stands for pound (libra), a unit of money
form is British slang for a criminal record

explanation.surface: A political policy and cash end up hidden by an Irishman who has a criminal record.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crimina!' is the OCR's reading of 'criminal'. Form is British slang for a police record, and Pat a stock Irish name.
explanation.definitionFit: A party's platform is its declared set of policies.

clue.text: Drop the odd units — see about a number

parts.note: rounding a number drops its odd units, as rounding 47 to 50

indicators.note: the word for see goes about, around, the letter a

parts.note: Ely is a cathedral city, a bishop's see

explanation.surface: Discarding spare units, see about a figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'see' means a bishop's diocese; Ely is an English cathedral city. 'number' is a song, not a figure.
explanation.definitionFit: A roundelay is a short song with a refrain, and a number is a piece of music.

clue.text: Return toys showing a blemish

indicators.note: return says the word for toys is sent back, read from end to start

parts.note: tops are spinning toys

explanation.surface: Toys handed back are seen to be flawed.
explanation.definitionFit: A spot is a small mark or blemish on the skin or a surface.

clue.text: Black and gold cocked hat

parts.note: sombre means dark or black

indicators.note: a cocked brim is turned up, so in this down clue the word for gold is turned upward

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: A black and gold tricorn hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cocked hat' is a phrase, but 'cocked' turns OR up to RO.
explanation.definitionFit: A sombrero is a broad-brimmed Mexican hat.

clue.text: Ancient academic institutions have neat tie

parts.note: neat is an old word for cattle, and an ox is one
a bridge ties two banks together

explanation.surface: Old universities have a tidy necktie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'neat tie' sounds like a tidy necktie; neat is old for cattle, giving OX.
explanation.definitionFit: Oxbridge names Oxford and Cambridge, England's oldest universities.

clue.text: Lacking a name once in a while

definitions.meaning: short for anonymous, of an unnamed author
an old word for now and then

explanation.surface: Something nameless turns up only occasionally.
explanation.definitionFit: Anon abbreviates anonymous, and as an archaic adverb means at times, as in 'ever and anon'.

clue.text: Trouble over run to third man, say. Appealing?

indicators.note: in a down clue over means the word for trouble sits above what follows
to joins the run onto the man that comes next

parts.note: ado is fuss or trouble
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

indicators.note: say means the name is spoken, giving a word that sounds like it

parts.note: Abel was the third human in Genesis, after Adam and Eve

explanation.surface: A cricket match: trouble over a run sent to the fielder at third man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'third man' looks like a cricket fielding position but is Abel, third human after Adam and Eve.
explanation.definitionFit: Something adorable is lovable and charming, which is appealing.

clue.text: Where label may be set down

definitions.text: Where label may be set down

parts.words: Where label may be set down
parts.note: a record label sits on a disc, and a thing set down officially is documented

explanation.surface: Asks where a label is to be written.
explanation.definitionFit: Something on record is formally documented, and a gramophone label is printed on the disc.

clue.text: Ruin cheat -start…

parts.note: to con someone is to cheat them
to found something is to start it up

explanation.surface: A fraud begins and ruins everything, the sentence running on into the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To confound is to defeat or bring to ruin, as in 'confound their plans'.

clue.text: Disorder I cannot keep in check

indicators.note: disorder means jumbled, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone admits being unable to keep turmoil under control.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disorder' rearranges the letters of I CANNOT.
explanation.definitionFit: To contain something is to restrain or hold it in check, as with anger.

clue.text: by protecting jilted girl's dignity

indicators.note: the word by wraps round and protects the girl's name
jilted suggests thrown over, so the girl's name is turned round

parts.note: Nora is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Continuing the last clue, a jilted girl's honour is shielded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jilted' turns the girl's name round, giving ARON. Read with the previous clue, the two make one sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: A barony is the rank of baron, a title or dignity of nobility.

clue.text: Neat, I'll say

definitions.meaning: neat is an old word for cattle, and this is a breed of them
the words I'll sound like isle, and this is a Channel Island

explanation.surface: Someone agrees emphatically that something is tidy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Neat' means cattle, an old sense; the Channel Island gives its name to a breed. 'I'll say' is heard as 'isle'.
explanation.definitionFit: Alderney is both a breed of dairy cattle and one of the Channel Islands off France.

clue.text: Stop listening and make love!

parts.note: an end is a stop or finish
to lend an ear is to be listening

explanation.surface: An exhortation to give up paying attention and make love instead.
explanation.definitionFit: To endear is to make someone loved or dear to others.

clue.text: This protects the ankle when footballer takes kick

indicators.note: the footballer takes, receiving the kick that follows him

parts.note: a half, such as a half-back, is a football position
to boot a ball is to kick it

explanation.surface: Ankle protection is needed when a footballer is kicked.
explanation.definitionFit: A half-boot is a boot reaching above the ankle, covering it.

clue.text: Variety of alder, one shrub with flowers

indicators.note: a variety is a different arrangement, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A type of alder is one flowering shrub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Variety of' rearranges the letters of ALDER and ONE.
explanation.definitionFit: The oleander is an evergreen shrub with showy pink or white blossoms.

clue.text: Heads you invented, tails we all invented sales returns

indicators.note: heads, as on a coin, are the first letters of the words that follow
tails, as on a coin, are the final letters of the words that follow

explanation.surface: Coin-tossing jargon about who invented what, ending in sales returns.
explanation.walkthrough: Heads and tails sound like a coin toss, but pick first letters of 'you invented' and final letters of 'we all invented sales'.
explanation.definitionFit: Yields are the returns an investment produces, such as interest or profit.
